title: LandlordGuard Dwelling Fire Policy Vacancy Permit — Desk Transaction Reference
content:
A landlord insured under the LandlordGuard Dwelling Fire Policy may request a vacancy permit for a rental building. A permit issued on the policy carries its first and last day on the policy record, and its charge is posted as one additional premium entry for the vacancy permit, dated the permit start, which raises the policy's premium balance by the charge.

## Situation of use and capability

`issue_vacancy_permit_2309bb3c` issues a vacancy permit on one LandlordGuard dwelling policy and posts its charge. One call writes the permit's first and last day onto the policy, so the vacancy permit shows on the policy from that moment, and posts one additional-premium entry for the vacancy permit, dated the permit's first day, that raises the policy's premium balance by the charge.

## How it is invoked

The tool is an agent-side tool. The representative unlocks it with `unlock_agent_discoverable_tool` and then calls it with `call_agent_discoverable_tool`, passing the tool name `issue_vacancy_permit_2309bb3c` and the parameters below.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `dwelling_policy_id` | the reference id of the landlord dwelling policy record the permit is issued on, as returned by the dwelling policy lookup for the verified caller | identifier |
| `permit_start` | the first day the permit covers | calendar date YYYY-MM-DD in the policy's local time zone; never empty |
| `permit_expiration` | the last day the permit covers; the permit covers this day | calendar date YYYY-MM-DD in the policy's local time zone; never empty |
| `charge` | the vacancy permit charge in USD | positive amount to 2 decimal places; a value with more places is rounded half-up to 2 decimal places when posted |

## Return

A one-line receipt: "Vacancy permit issued: entry <entry_id> on policy <dwelling_policy_id>, permit <permit_start> to <permit_expiration>, charge <charge> USD posted <posted_date>." The entry id is the new premium-ledger entry, the permit dates are YYYY-MM-DD, the charge is shown to 2 decimal places and the posted date is the current date. Receiving this line means the permit and its charge are recorded; the permit dates are then visible on the policy and the charge on its premium account.

## Hypothetical illustration

For a hypothetical policy reference DWP-EXAMPLE, a permit from 2025-03-03 through 2025-05-31 with a charge of 90.00 would be passed as `dwelling_policy_id` DWP-EXAMPLE, `permit_start` 2025-03-03, `permit_expiration` 2025-05-31 and `charge` 90.00, and the receipt would echo those dates and the amount.
